races.name: RF Miller & Co Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
Hadwins Mares' Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Fair Damsel
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner in the race; Danny Gilligan takes the ride and the pace data gives her a clear lead by default — the STYLE_FIT flag reflects she is genuinely suited here, but the discount applies if she is outpaced early; 41 days off is not a concern given her Good-ground form and the p-headgear note.

runners_data.name: Victoria Milano
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up mare for Greenall & Guerriero with solid Good-ground form including a second and third at 23f and 20f — her five-run sequence on similar going reads encouragingly, though her H style means she is reliant on a strong enough gallop to close down.

runners_data.name: Belles Benefit
runners_data.note: Ben Case sends her out after a long 236-day absence wearing blinkers; she has winning form on Good ground at 26f and 22f and races prominently, making her a live each-way contender if her fitness is spot-on — the layoff is the key question mark.

runners_data.name: Blackwater Lilly
runners_data.note: Neil King's six-year-old has been consistently placed on Good ground at shorter trips; she races from hold-up and will need to improve significantly on the clock to peg back the leaders at 2m6f — her best form is over a shorter distance range of 17-18f.

runners_data.name: Gerrys Wish
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen, a top-tier jockey booking, rides for Gordon Elliott and races prominently — that partnership commands respect and the yard is in strong form (8/45 in 14 days); her record on Good shows three places from nine runs, but she has yet to win on this surface.

runners_data.name: Turkey And Ham
runners_data.note: Amateur jockey (5lb claim) for Irish yard Noel C Kelly; races with tongue-strap and hood headgear, suggesting she needs restraining — won at 18f on Good last season and stays the 2m6f trip; 67-day break is mildly concerning but headgear combination may sharpen her.

runners_data.name: Parish Star
runners_data.note: Adam Nicol's five-year-old arrives in form having been placed in four of her last five starts; she races from hold-up but the small trainer (3/7 in 14 days shows activity) and apprentice rider Joshua Thompson (5lb) keep costs down — her best Good-going form came at 20f, shorter than today's trip.

runners_data.name: Forest Spirit
runners_data.note: Good recent second at 20f on Soft for Mickey Bowen, but her natural inclination is to race held up at the back — placed in midfield on the map because the field is saturated with hold-up types, meaning she is unlikely to get as far back as she ideally wants and may race in an uncomfortable middle-ground position.

runners_data.name: Alvesta
runners_data.note: Scored most recently at 17f on Good for George Bewley and Brian Hughes; her hold-up style is her natural mode, but with several other hold-up types in the field she too is mapped forward of her true position — Hughes is a top-class conditional who may find a clever route through, though the pace scenario must suit.

runners_data.name: Masonbrook Meadow
runners_data.note: Seamus Mullins' five-year-old ran second over 24f on Good last time and clearly stays this trip; as with the other redistributed hold-up horses, the overcrowding at the rear means she is unlikely to get the covered-up, late-run race she needs — Benjamin Macey (5lb) is an unknown quantity in a big field.

races.paceDynamic: Fair Damsel is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she can dictate a measured, sustainable gallop around Cartmel's tight 2m6f circuit on Good ground — a setup that plays directly into her hands. Gerrys Wish, Belles Benefit, and Turkey And Ham will press forward prominently behind her, creating a small cluster of pace but not enough to seriously pressurise Fair Damsel at the head of affairs. The hold-up brigade — Victoria Milano, Blackwater Lilly, Parish Star — will be forced to hunt from the rear, but with only a modest pace being set they face the classic problem of a gap that may never open wide enough for them to bridge in time. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers and the front-runner specifically, as a controlled tempo on Good ground at Cartmel rewards those who travel handy and can quicken from the front of the field in the home straight. Three runners (Forest Spirit, Alvesta, Masonbrook Meadow) are genuine hold-up types redistributed to midfield on the map because the field holds more hold-up horses than can all settle at the rear; of those, Forest Spirit and Alvesta are most likely to find a midfield pitch, though their true preference for being covered up may leave them stranded if the pace is as sedate as the race shape suggests.

scenarios.trigger: If a cluster of prominent horses contest the lead vigorously early, drastically elevating the tempo and causing multiple horses to capitulate.
scenarios.body: If a cluster of prominent horses contest the lead vigorously early, drastically elevating the tempo and causing multiple horses to capitulate.

watchPoints.text: Fair Damsel is the lone pace-setter and if she gets an uncontested lead she can dictate terms throughout — watch whether any of the prominent trio (Gerrys Wish, Belles Benefit, Turkey And Ham) pushes up to pressurise her early, as that is the single biggest factor that could change the race shape entirely.

Belles Benefit has been off for 236 days and runs in blinkers for Ben Case — horses returning from long absences over hurdles can jump sketchily on their first run back, and if she makes errors it could compromise both her own race and those immediately behind her.

The three redistributed hold-up horses (Forest Spirit, Alvesta, Masonbrook Meadow) will all be jockeying for a similar position in the early stages; watch for crowding and shuffling on the first bend at Cartmel, which is a notoriously tight track where position is difficult to recover.

Sean Bowen on Gerrys Wish is a significant jockey booking for Gordon Elliott — if the pair are sent forward to press Fair Damsel they could transform this from a dawdle into a genuine test, altering the outcome for every hold-up runner in the field.

Good ground is confirmed across the card at Cartmel today — no horse has a going concern, but horses with the most extensive Good-ground histories (Blackwater Lilly with 10 runs, Belles Benefit and Gerrys Wish with 9) carry the most reliable form lines into this race.

races.name: Molson Coors Novices' Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Settle Down Jill
runners_data.note: Strong Cartmel profile with two wins from 15 starts on similar going; races prominently under Harry Reed for in-form Tristan Davidson (2/8 over 14 days), and a return to Good ground after recent Soft outings suits — best positioned to capitalise if Passengerontheship wavers.

runners_data.name: Passengerontheship
runners_data.note: Four-timer on the line and the race's sole genuine front-runner, with all four wins coming on Good ground; Jonathan England for Sam England (4/15 T14) can dictate every yard, and the tongue-tie hints at a horse that needs to be kept busy — only five days since last run is worth monitoring for freshness.

runners_data.name: Back In The Bay
runners_data.note: Jonathan Burke takes over on a horse with two wins on Good ground at this trip, but a hold-up style leaves him reliant on the pace collapsing at Cartmel — a track that historically punishes late runners; the 34-day absence since his last start (a well-beaten seventh) adds a small query.

runners_data.name: Justicialism
runners_data.note: Consistent second-place finisher (three runner-up spots in last five) but carries an official fade-in-finish flag that is damaging in a race where the leader controls tempo; Mr D McGill's 5lb claim provides modest compensation, and the trainer's 0/4 over 14 days offers no confidence boost.

runners_data.name: Aslukgoes
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen takes the ride for Mickey Bowen on a horse who has won four times on similar going but whose recent form reads P476-4; fitted with a hood and racing prominently, he should be close enough to be involved but needs a bigger performance than those recent efforts suggest.

runners_data.name: Jack Sprat
runners_data.note: Veteran of consistent placed efforts but his true hold-up style means he is operating out of his natural position in a six-runner field where the rear is crowded; the STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) tempers expectations, and a latest run of ninth suggests the form may not be at its peak regardless of positioning.

races.paceDynamic: Passengerontheship is the sole confirmed front-runner and arrives on the back of four consecutive wins, giving Jonathan England every reason to send him straight to the front and dictate from the outset on Good ground at Cartmel. With only Settle Down Jill and Aslukgoes likely to challenge for early prominent positions, the pace is set to be honest but uncontested at the head, meaning Passengerontheship controls tempo entirely on his own terms over this 2m5f trip. The hold-up brigade of Back In The Bay, Justicialism, and Jack Sprat will be forced to work from further back, and with Cartmel's sharp, undulating nature limiting late-run opportunities, those off the pace face a stiff task unless the leader fades markedly. This race shape strongly favours the front-running and prominent profiles — a single dominant pace-setter dictating a sustainable gallop on a track that rewards those travelling well throughout rather than those producing one late burst.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Passengerontheship Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Passengerontheship leads at a controlled, sustainable pace and is never seriously pressed by Settle Down Jill or Aslukgoes.
scenarios.body: If Passengerontheship leads at a controlled, sustainable pace and is never seriously pressed by Settle Down Jill or Aslukgoes.

scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Press Hard
scenarios.trigger: If Settle Down Jill and Aslukgoes push forward aggressively and force a genuinely contested gallop from the outset.
scenarios.body: If Settle Down Jill and Aslukgoes push forward aggressively and force a genuinely contested gallop from the outset.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace burns out the leaders and a closer produces a strong finishing run down the Cartmel straight.
scenarios.body: If the pace burns out the leaders and a closer produces a strong finishing run down the Cartmel straight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart — Errors & Attrition
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or early departures among the front pair disrupt the race shape and hand the race to whoever survives cleanest.
scenarios.body: If jumping errors or early departures among the front pair disrupt the race shape and hand the race to whoever survives cleanest.

watchPoints.text: Passengerontheship's five-day turnaround and tongue-tie combination — watch for any signs of over-exuberance early or jumping fatigue in the closing stages if he has not fully recovered.

Settle Down Jill vs Aslukgoes for the prominent pitch — if both push forward hard to track Passengerontheship, the early gallop could become more genuinely contested than the single front-runner map suggests.

Back In The Bay's hold-up profile at Cartmel — watch where Jonathan Burke settles him in the first half-mile, as getting too far back on this tight track could render his finishing effort irrelevant regardless of stamina.

Justicialism's fade flag is worth monitoring at the business end — if he appears to travel well turning in but fails to pick up, it confirms the pattern and eliminates him from contention early in the straight.

Jack Sprat's positional reality — watch whether Brian Hughes attempts to place him closer than expected given the small field; if so, his redistributed mapping becomes less of a concern, though recent form remains uninspiring.

races.name: Lakes Luxury Loo's Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Caughtinyourtrance
runners_data.note: Lone pace-setter here with clear tactical control; Brian Hughes teams up with James Moffatt (2/12 T14 form) and the horse carries tp headgear, but a STYLE_FIT flag and recent form of 23P-22 tempers confidence despite its prominent profile being perfectly placed in this race.|

runners_data.name: Red Happy
runners_data.note: Three wins from five on Good ground (sim-going 6/15, 3W) and a recent run of back-to-back victories before a subsequent pair of refusals raises a concern — connections will need it to have its jumping head on, but if it does, Jonathon Bewley and George Bewley's runner arrives with outstanding Good-ground credentials at this trip.|

runners_data.name: Stratagem
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old with a solid trainer in Mickey Bowen (5/30 T14) and a reliable recent record including wins at 3m on Good; amateur Mr James Murray takes a 7lb claim which partially offsets the OR, and headgear (tp) suggests connections are trying to optimise focus over this genuinely stamina-testing 3m1½f.|

runners_data.name: Tiger Orchid
runners_data.note: The one genuine hold-up horse in the field; Charlie Hammond has a consistent mount with 12 of 15 Good-ground runs placing, and the horse's form of 222-31 shows recent improvement — needs the pace to be honest enough to close into, which is not guaranteed given Caughtinyourtrance's likely control.|

runners_data.name: Ivane
runners_data.note: Carries visor headgear and James Owen's operation has been busy (6/51 T14); though naturally a prominent racer, the surplus of handy types means Jonathan Burke will likely find himself in a less-than-ideal slot, and a form string of 4264-4 offers little reason to be confident even if it does get the position it wants.|

runners_data.name: Fairlawn Flyer
runners_data.note: Mickey Bowen saddles this one alongside stablemate Stratagem — Sean Bowen takes the ride, which is the key upgrade angle; naturally wants to bowl along up front but the race simply has no room for it there, and a pulled-up run at 32f on Soft and a recent OR of 115 suggest it is being asked to operate at the limit of its effective distance.|

runners_data.name: Le Grand Vert
runners_data.note: Won last time out (1/25f/GOO, 20 days ago) and arrives the freshest in the field; Noel C Kelly's runner is realistically a mid-pack participant in this shape despite preferring to race prominently, and Mr O McGill's 5lb claim could matter if the race falls apart — the back-to-back 1 and 4 form on Good warrants a token each-way consideration.|

races.paceDynamic: Caughtinyourtrance is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival for the lead, will dictate a controlled, unhurried gallop around Cartmel's tight 3m1½f circuit on Good ground. The field is loaded with prominent-type runners — Ivane, Fairlawn Flyer, and Le Grand Vert all want to race handy but cannot all occupy that position, meaning at least some of them will be shuffled wider or further back than they prefer, adding friction early without necessarily forcing a genuinely fast pace. Red Happy and Stratagem are the most likely to secure the front rank behind Caughtinyourtrance given their recent form and claiming/amateur jockey dynamic on Fairlawn Flyer and Le Grand Vert, while Tiger Orchid is the one genuine hold-up horse who can afford to settle and produce a finish from the back. This race shape — a single uncontested pace-setter, sustainable fractions, a messy mid-pack — strongly favours a prominent horse who travels smoothly just off the leader and picks up cleanly in the straight, with Tiger Orchid's hold-up style a secondary beneficiary if the pace is genuinely compressed. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can realistically claim those positions; Caughtinyourtrance, Red Happy, and Stratagem are best-placed to actually secure the ground they want, while Ivane, Fairlawn Flyer, and Le Grand Vert face a race that may not be run to suit them.

scenarios.body: If Caughtinyourtrance sets an uncontested, moderate gallop and the race is run at a steady tempo throughout.

scenarios.body: If the cluster of prominent types creates enough early bustle that the early fractions are slightly elevated, flattening the front pair.

scenarios.trigger: If the overcrowded prominent group causes interference, jumping errors, or mid-race reshuffling that opens the race up unexpectedly.
scenarios.body: If the overcrowded prominent group causes interference, jumping errors, or mid-race reshuffling that opens the race up unexpectedly.

watchPoints.text: Caughtinyourtrance controls the pace entirely unchallenged — if Brian Hughes finds a flawless jumping rhythm and no one tests it in the back straight, it could prove very hard to catch despite the STYLE_FIT caveat.
Red Happy's back-to-back refusals (R-R in recent form) are a live jumping safety concern — watch how it settles at the first fence, as a repeat would decimate punters at a race with only 7 runners.

Fairlawn Flyer and Le Grand Vert will both be pushed wider or further back than they prefer at the start — watch for early crowding or interference between these two and Ivane as they compete for positions they cannot all fill.

Tiger Orchid's closing ability hinges entirely on whether the tempo is genuine enough — watch the pace through the back straight on the second circuit; if Caughtinyourtrance is still going easily with a clear lead, Tiger Orchid's late run may simply run out of track on Cartmel's short straight.

Stratagem is backed by the in-form Bowen/Bowen pairing at Cartmel (Mickey Bowen T14 5/30) — watch for Mr James Murray to position it smartly off Caughtinyourtrance's shoulder from an early stage, as the 7lb claim could prove decisive in a steady-run race where weight matters late.

races.name: Holker Homes Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: Thank You Blue
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who has won on soft and shown prominent form on good, but recent similar-going form reads 0 wins and 0 places from 9 runs on comparable surfaces — the STYLE_FIT tag here reflects that forcing a front-running role from a naturally prominent-preferring horse could limit finishing reserves late.|

runners_data.name: Blue Reed
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 19f on Good ground for a trainer whose yard is 1 from 10 in the past 14 days — in good form and this distance/going combination suits; naturally wants to race prominently and should secure that position comfortably here.|

runners_data.name: Zumbi
runners_data.note: Has won and placed repeatedly in recent starts, including a win over 18f on Good and a second over 21f on Good — the trip and conditions are squarely in his comfort zone, and he carries a tongue-tie that he has worn in his placed efforts.|

runners_data.name: Am Still Here
runners_data.note: 266 days off the track is the key flag here — Nicky Richards is a trainer who has form returning horses fresh, and this five-year-old's entire recent profile is placed efforts on soft and good, suggesting she handles the surface; naturally prominent and Sean Quinlan gives her every chance if fitness is there.|

runners_data.name: Tell Me Again
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up type whose last eight runs on Good ground show 0 wins and just 1 place from 10 — going is fine but Cartmel's track does not suit horses needing a strong pace collapse; Micky Hammond's yard has been busy but this profile looks vulnerable in a controlled-pace scenario.|

runners_data.name: Judicial Review
runners_data.note: Won over 21f on Good but that was some time back — a genuine prominent runner by nature whose true position has been redistributed to midfield on this map because the prominent slots are congested; Brian Hughes rides for James Moffatt (0 from 3 in last 14 days) and this horse will need things to go wrong up front to get competitive.|

runners_data.name: Out On Her Own
runners_data.note: Consistent placer with five seconds and thirds from her last seven runs on Good and soft — Ryan Mania is a positive booking and she clearly handles this ground, but as a genuine hold-up operator she needs the front group to crack, which this pace map does not strongly support.|

runners_data.name: Roi Du Roume
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen's booking elevates this one's profile — placed at Cartmel-type tracks over 2m4f on Good, but his last five runs show 0 wins and 1 place and he tends to run his race from the rear; this shape does not naturally bring him into the finish.|

runners_data.name: Mr Globalist
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse whose true rearward position has been absorbed into the midfield map due to redistribution — has placed five times in his last fifteen runs on Good but without a win; the STYLE_FIT note applies and his role here is likely to be filling the places at best rather than challenging for the spoils.|

runners_data.name: On The Platform
runners_data.note: NON-RUNNER — flagged as such in the data and must be discounted entirely from race analysis; was a natural prominent type and his absence further reduces pressure on Thank You Blue at the head of affairs.|

races.paceDynamic: Thank You Blue is the confirmed front-runner and will dictate from the front, setting a sustainable gallop over 2m5f on Good ground at Cartmel — a track where controlling the pace from the front carries genuine tactical value. Blue Reed, Zumbi, and Am Still Here are all natural prominent racers who will press to sit just behind, creating a compact front group but not a truly contested, burning pace that blows the field apart. The race is likely to be run at an honest but manageable tempo, which will reward horses that can travel fluently in the first half and sustain their effort over the final circuit — a profile that suits prominent racers with proven stamina on Good ground. Closers who need a true test to make up ground from the rear are disadvantaged by the lack of genuine pressure on the leader. The field contains more prominent-running types than can all secure their favoured positions — Judicial Review and On The Platform are natural front-rank horses pushed onto the map further back, with Thank You Blue, Blue Reed, and Zumbi best placed to actually dominate the prominent berths.

watchPoints.text: Thank You Blue's sustainable pace from the front is the defining factor — if he is allowed to bowl along unchallenged, Blue Reed and Zumbi shadowing him without pressure are the direct threats to his dominance late on.

Am Still Here returns after 266 days off and is unproven fresh — watch the market for late confidence from the Nicky Richards yard, as a well-backed returning runner at a price would shift scenario probabilities toward Scenario D.

Judicial Review is a genuine prominent runner squeezed onto the midfield map — if Brian Hughes pushes forward aggressively early and reclaims a tracking position, this horse's profile improves materially and Scenario B becomes more likely.

On The Platform is a non-runner — his absence removes one prominent-type competitor and makes it marginally easier for Blue Reed and Zumbi to secure their natural front-rank positions without a crowded early berth.|

races.name: Cartmel Priory Cofe School Amateur Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Garrick Painter
runners_data.note: True hold-up performer whose recent form shows a win over 16f on Good but a tendency to fade late, which in a modestly-run race is a significant risk; 41 days fresh and a 168lb burden add to his vulnerabilities on this tight track.

runners_data.name: Envious Editor
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old returning from 420 days off (33 days post-point-to-point) who is at heart a hold-up horse carrying a tongue-tie, mapped to midfield simply because the field is stacked with similar types — his chance is heavily conditioned by whether a genuine pace develops to close into.

runners_data.name: Lightening Company
runners_data.note: Has winning form on Good ground over similar trips but is 307 days since last completing a race (last outing a pull-up), making fitness a real concern; at eight years old he is a hold-up type who needs to be treated with caution until shown to retain his level.

runners_data.name: Jolie Coeur Allen
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with multiple wins and places over 17f on Good ground, making him one of the better-placed runners for course and going; 99 days since last run and trainer Ben Haslam in modest recent form, but this is arguably his race shape if any pace materialises.

runners_data.name: Dog Fox
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner who has 13 of 15 career runs on similar going and is entirely at home on Good, making him the key pace-controlling force; jockey Miss Heraghty on a 7lb claim is a factor, and his style-fit note is a reminder he may not face the pressure needed to stretch the field.

runners_data.name: Goodwin Face
runners_data.note: Progressive six-year-old prominent racer with four top-three finishes on Good ground, and importantly has course form at this trip; trained by Chris Gordon who is 0/5 in the last 14 days, but Goodwin Face's position just off the pace makes him the most natural challenger to Dog Fox.

runners_data.name: Book Of Secrets
runners_data.note: Consistent but modest performer whose last five runs have all produced finishes between fourth and eighth; a true hold-up horse pushed into the midfield map position because there are simply too many hold-up types in the race, and his 0-from-15 record on similar going is damning.

runners_data.name: Dusky Days
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old who has placed twice on Good ground but over much longer trips (22-26f), raising a genuine distance concern over this 2m1f; racing out of his natural hold-up role, this is a tricky ask.

runners_data.name: Zamond
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old prominent racer with Good-ground wins who was beaten eight lengths last time but has competitive recent form; Donald McCain's 2/26 in 14 days is a moderate yard strike-rate and the age is a minor concern, but he has the positional profile to be involved.

runners_data.name: Out Out
runners_data.note: Five-year-old Dan Skelton-trained horse returning from a 441-day absence (404 days since his last point-to-point), making fitness almost impossible to gauge; only 1 win from 7 on similar going and genuinely a hold-up type who is unlikely to reproduce his best first time back.

runners_data.name: Blue Siam
runners_data.note: Four-year-old non-runner — effectively not in the race; listed for completeness but should be disregarded from all tactical calculations.

races.paceDynamic: Dog Fox is the sole confirmed front-runner in this field and, facing no genuine rival for the lead, will likely dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front around Cartmel's tight, undulating 2m1f circuit. Goodwin Face and Zamond are the natural prominent types who will look to track Dog Fox through the early stages, creating a small group up front with the remainder strung out behind. The pace is unlikely to be truly searching — a lone leader setting an honest but uncontested tempo on Good ground generally means the race is not run at a clip that strips out the field early, leaving a premium on horses travelling well in the slipstream rather than those making relentless late ground. This shape strongly favours prominent racers and close trackers who can pounce turning in, rather than genuine hold-up horses needing a strong pace to close into. Envious Editor, Book Of Secrets, Dusky Days, Out Out and Blue Siam are all true hold-up types redistributed to midfield on the map because there are far more hold-up horses in this field than the race shape can accommodate at the rear; Dog Fox, Goodwin Face and Zamond are those most likely to actually secure their natural forward positions.

watchPoints.text: Watch Dog Fox's jumping throughout — if he makes a significant error at any of Cartmel's early hurdles and loses his position, the entire pace scenario collapses and the race becomes chaotic with no confirmed leader.

Goodwin Face's jockey Mr Henry Main (5lb claimer) has the task of deciding whether to press Dog Fox or sit and track — if he overcommits too early on this tight track, he risks emptying before the final hurdle.
Envious Editor's 420-day absence (including a point-to-point 33 days ago) is a major fitness concern; if he tires mid-race and takes up ground, he could impede horses trying to close from behind.

Jolie Coeur Allen's trainer Ben Haslam has two runners in this race (also Lightening Company) — watch for any market move that might indicate which horse the stable is more confident about entering the final furlong.

The cluster of seven-pound claimer jockeys across multiple runners means small positional errors early on Cartmel's tight bends could be amplified — watch the first bend for crowding that could affect the midfield hold-up horses' ability to find a rhythm.
